handoff.prompt:
Distil the durable lessons from Quarter Turn's first build. Project root is /Users/erickanney/builder/projects/quarter-turn — work only there for project knowledge, and propose kit-wide lessons as files in `~/builder/.claude/knowledge/inbox/` rather than editing the kit KB.

The run logs are in `wiki/runs/` and `wiki/daily/2026-08-26.md`; the git history (27 commits, each a verified unit with a body explaining why) is the other main source and is worth reading — several commit bodies record a decision and the reasoning behind it deliberately.

What this build was: a 3x3x3 Rubik's cube PWA, built in one session from intake through gates. 237 tests, detector clean, code review and QA and the image gate all run. It deliberately does NOT follow the kit's Hono/Drizzle backend convention — `architecture` ruled at intake that a single-player on-device app does not earn it — so it is a static PWA with IndexedDB.

**Candidates I think are kit-wide, but judge them yourself rather than taking my framing:**

1. **The image gate has a blind spot, and two tools stacked to hide it.** `bin/gen-image.mjs` checks for "transparency requested but not delivered" and has nothing for the reverse. The provider returned a PNG with real alpha across half the canvas when `transparent: false` was requested — and `bin/image-check.mjs` passed it clean, because its uniform-border-band detector needs opaque pixels to measure and simply does not fire against a transparent surround. So the margin defect it was meant to catch was still there and had become invisible. Two attempts with identical transparency requests differed on this, so it is provider non-determinism, not something a prompt controls. The fix that worked was a deterministic post-process, not a fourth generation. Separately: `image-check.mjs` does not scan subdirectories, so a derived icon set under `public/icons/` reports "0 assets" — which reads exactly like passing.

2. **A backgrounded browser pane makes a whole class of interaction unverifiable, and it fails silently.** `requestAnimationFrame` does not run in a hidden tab. Any interaction whose commit happens at the END of an animation — a drag that springs into place, a sequence that plays out — can therefore be driven, appear to work, and never commit, with no error anywhere. Injecting the clock and frame scheduler into the gesture layer turned the single most important interaction in this app from unverifiable-by-watching into seven deterministic tests. That may generalise to any canvas or gesture work.

3. **Following an optimal-ish solver one step at a time can cycle forever.** A two-phase solver is deterministic per state but not optimal, so its first move from state S can lead to a state whose own first move returns to S. Re-solving on every hint request produced the same move forever. Plan once, serve the plan in order, recompute only on divergence. The general shape — one-step-at-a-time advice from a deterministic non-optimal planner is not guaranteed to converge — may be worth naming.

4. **Research can be confidently wrong in a way only building reveals.** The grounded WCA research told me to detect CFOP stage boundaries by scanning backward for the last continuously-true moment, to avoid a stage flickering true by coincidence. Every last-layer algorithm breaks F2L partway through and restores it, so a backward scan reports F2L complete from inside the last-layer algorithm on every real solve. The finding it was guarding against was real; the fix was wrong. I corrected the spec alongside the code.

5. **I ran `qa` against the app while still editing it.** Its report carried a React crash and one mislabelled record that were both HMR churn from my concurrent edits, and it correctly flagged them as needing a clean re-check rather than asserting them. It cost a re-verification pass. Serialising the gate against the code is probably the rule.

Project-level knowledge worth keeping for whoever opens this app next: why the cube engine is rotations rather than facelet permutation tables, why the hint plans, why stage detection scans forward, why the icon has a normalizer, and what the `dist/web/ui/` primitives are (unused — the chrome is bespoke).

Be sceptical. Some of these are one-off, some are already covered in the pitfalls files — check before proposing, and say which you rejected and why.

**Project wiki** (`wiki/learnings.md` was empty): three entries — the approved no-backend-convention deviation and why it shouldn't be quietly reversed or quietly kept without re-checking; that `dist/web/ui/` is genuinely unused (bespoke game chrome instead), so a future session doesn't mistake that for a gap; and the `window.__quarterTurn` dev handle, which is this app's specific answer to the rAF/hidden-tab QA problem and isn't written down anywhere else.

The durable knowledge from this build now lives in `wiki/learnings.md` (project-specific), `src/app.md` and `.builder-plan.md` (decisions with their reasoning, already complete), and the three inbox proposals above (kit-wide, pending `kit-review`).
